Do you hear that? The constant gunfire? The shelling? And they tell the world there is a ceasefire? There is no pause. No reprieve. No safety for Palestinians in Gaza. On October 11, our team visited families whose tents had been burned, leaving them without shelter once again. Even as we filmed, heavy gunfire echoed around us. This is the reality of life in Gaza. Families who have lost everything continue to live under the threat of violence, yet refuse to be driven from their land. This is what steadfastness looks like. Sumud. A determination that is difficult to comprehend unless you understand what it means to face the loss of your homeland. They have burned their shelters, destroyed their neighborhoods, and displaced them again and again. But they have not broken their connection to Palestine. They are not leaving. They are not surrendering their right to exist on their land. Help support them. The Sameer Project is one of the only organizations that delivers aid in these danger zones. Give to our Food and Water Campaign .

It’s been nine months since I left Gaza. People often think that once you make it out, the suffering ends. It doesn’t. Some days, it feels like it never left. We’re still living with the consequences of that dark day!October 7. The grief didn’t stay behind in Gaza. It followed us. This morning, I lost another one of my cats. She was hit by a car right in front of my home. She’s the eighth out of my nine cats that I’ve lost. Sometimes it feels like life just keeps finding new ways to break what’s left of my heart.. #rip #rest #loss #🐾

Votes are still being counted in Israel's first election since 7 October 2023, with no clear winner yet determined. But, exit polls and partial official results show that Palestinian parties will dramatically increase their representation in the Israeli Knesset. Predictions are they could win as many as 19 seats, making them the kingmakers in negotiations to form a new government. While neither the current prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s far-right coalition, nor the opposition bloc led by the former general Gadi Eisenkot, have won enough seats, experts have said that if Eisenkot falls short of a majority, he would be obliged to sit down to talk with the Palestinian groupings, the Joint List and Ra’am, to try to form a government, which could take weeks. Most of the Jewish opposition parties in the Change bloc anchored by Eisenkot have rejected the idea of working with Palestinian-Israeli parties. "The big gains made by Palestinian parties in Israel’s general election pose an urgent and fundamental challenge to the country’s mainstream opposition: either cooperate with Arab Israelis or hand Benjamin Netanyahu a roadmap to political survival," writes the Guardian’s senior international correspondent, Julian Borger. Palestinian Christians are not newcomers to the Holy Land. Our roots trace back to the very beginnings of Christianity.  For centuries, Christian communities have endured persecution and hardship, from periods of oppression following the Islamic conquests to violence and intimidation by Islamist extremist groups, and today, suffering amid Isr@eli military operations, settler violence, and displacement. Through it all, our churches, liturgies, and faith have endured. These are not just historical sites. They are living Christian communities, families, and generations who have called the Holy Land home. Please keep the Christians of Palestine in your prayers.
